clue.text: Roman poet tries to win initially in military tribunals

indicators.note: this word tells you the wooing piece is placed at the start, before the poet

parts.note: to court someone is to try to win their favour or hand
Martial was a Roman poet famous for his epigrams

explanation.surface: A Roman poet faces charges before military judges, trying to win his case.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the poet first, but 'initially' says the wooing word comes at the front of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Courts formed by the armed forces to try service members are military tribunals.

clue.text: Criminal relation missing end of case at court?

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of the next word are bent out of shape and rearranged
missing tells you a letter is taken out of the word relation
end of picks the final letter of the word case

explanation.surface: A crooked relative, lacking only the end of the case, waits at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of case' is E; 'missing' removes it from RELATION, leaving RLATION, which 'Criminal' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone being tried in a courtroom is said to be facing justice there, before judge and jury.

clue.text: Staff coach going round a huge lorry

indicators.note: going round shows the staff piece encircling the letter given by a

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
a coach is a railway carriage, and to coach is to train; here a train

explanation.surface: Staff on a coach trip circle a giant truck.
explanation.walkthrough: A ROAD TRAIN is an Australian term for a lorry towing several trailers.
explanation.definitionFit: A long articulated truck pulling multiple trailers across the outback is a giant lorry.

clue.text: Way Satchmo, say, attains US city

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
Satchmo was the nickname of jazz trumpeter Louis Armstrong

explanation.surface: Louis Armstrong makes his way to an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attains' is a link joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A major Missouri metropolis on the Mississippi is a city of the United States.

clue.text: Hermit Saint appearing in excellent movement

indicators.note: appearing in puts the saint's letter inside the word for excellent

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent
a tic is an involuntary twitching movement

explanation.surface: A holy recluse shows up in a fine piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks musical but is the twitch TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who lives in austere self-denial, like a recluse, is called this.

clue.text: Produce I dropped turning up in grass

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the remaining letters are read from bottom to top
dropped tells you the letter I is removed from the word for produce

parts.note: fruit is produce, as in farm produce

explanation.surface: Some produce I dropped turns up lying in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping I from FRUIT leaves FRUT, which 'turning up' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Short grass with its matted roots, as in a lawn or racecourse, is sod.

clue.text: Illness resulting from slight adulteration of food

indicators.note: a slight adulteration signals that the letters of a word for food are mixed a little

parts.note: aliment is an old word for food or nourishment

explanation.surface: Sickness caused by slightly tainted food.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'slight' adulteration swaps just two letters of ALIMENT, the L and the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorder or sickness, often minor, is a complaint of the body.

clue.text: Where oil leaks may occur later on

explanation.surface: Oil leaks from a pipe that will come later.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally inside a conduit carrying oil, and figuratively something planned and on its way soon.

clue.text: Drinkers timed out in this town

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Pub-goers get their time called in this town.
explanation.walkthrough: KIDDERMINSTER is a town in Worcestershire, England, known for carpets. 'timed out' hints at last orders being called in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is an English town, named here as 'this town'.

clue.text: Take note of everything involving the French and sport

indicators.note: involving shows the note-and-everything pieces wrapping round the French word

parts.note: NB, nota bene, means take note
et is the French word for and
all means everything

explanation.surface: Notice everything about the French and their sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French and' is a slightly odd phrase: it means the French word for 'and'. 'involving' places it straight after the first letter of the note.
explanation.definitionFit: A team ball game played mainly by women, where players shoot at a raised ring, is a sport.

clue.text: Composer about to be nipped by tailless dog

indicators.note: nipped by shows the word for about caught between the dog's jaws
tailless removes the last letter of the dog's name

parts.note: a collie is a breed of dog
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A composer is about to get bitten by a dog with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: COLLIE loses its tail E to give COLLI, which holds RE. Corelli was an Italian Baroque composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque violinist and writer of concertos, a composer.

clue.text: Stones one set in sword handle finally cut

indicators.note: set in places the letter for one inside the shortened handle
finally cut removes the last letter of the word for sword handle

parts.note: the hilt is a sword's handle
a is one

explanation.surface: Gemstones set in a sword's handle are finally cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' sounds like gems, given the sword, but here means hailstones; HILT loses its final T to give HIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellets of ice falling from the sky are called hailstones, or simply stones.

clue.text: Go off and join the children quickly

explanation.surface: Someone leaves to go and catch up with the kids fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Seed means offspring, so hurrying to them is running to seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To deteriorate, as a plant bolting does; and literally to hurry towards one's offspring.

clue.text: See 13
See 3 down
This red phosphorus I compounded in laboratory vessel

indicators.note: compounded suggests chemicals mixed together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A chemist mixes red phosphorus in a lab container.
explanation.walkthrough: Red phosphorus is a real chemical, which keeps the lab picture neat.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow round glass container used to grow bacteria cultures is a laboratory vessel.

clue.text: City acting as home to nearly historic star

indicators.note: acting as home to shows the city housing the shortened word

parts.note: Paris is a city

indicators.note: nearly takes the final letter off the word for historic

parts.note: old means historic

explanation.surface: A city that houses an almost historic star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acting as home to' reads like theatre talk, but it means the city contains the trimmed word, just after its first letter. Polaris is the Pole Star.
explanation.definitionFit: The bright star at the end of the Little Bear's tail is the Pole Star.

clue.text: City entertainment enthralling good man

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the saint is held within the entertainment word

parts.note: cheer can mean food and drink, entertainment, as in good cheer
St, a saint, is a good man in crosswords

explanation.surface: A city's entertainment captivates a good man.
explanation.walkthrough: CHESTER is a walled cathedral city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is an English city in Cheshire.

clue.text: Page's last line, say, yet to be reached?

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
the last line of a story is an example of its ending

explanation.surface: The final line of the page has not been reached yet.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a loose reading: something awaiting an outcome is yet to be reached.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awaiting a decision or outcome, still undecided, is said to be this.

clue.text: Cooked hot flan? Yes, please!

indicators.note: cooked suggests letters prepared and changed, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Asked if they want a hot flan, someone eagerly accepts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang meaning 'very much so', an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: This British exclamation means 'definitely', an eager acceptance of an offer.

clue.text: State borders of Greece or borders of Gambia will hold one

indicators.note: borders of picks the first and last letters of the word Greece
will hold shows the Gambian borders holding the numeral inside
borders of picks the first and last letters of the word Gambia

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nation's frontiers with Greece or Gambia will hold one.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of Gambia are G and A, which surround I. Georgia is both a US state and a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia is a US state and also a nation in the Caucasus.

clue.text: Car to go wrong in remote Italy

indicators.note: in shows the word for going wrong set inside the word for remote

parts.note: far means remote
to err is to go wrong
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A car breaks down in a remote part of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ferrari is the Italian sports-car maker, which fits the Italian setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ferrari is an Italian sports car.

clue.text: Flower, unconfined, is coming up all over Austria

indicators.note: all over says these pieces sit on top of the next letter in the down entry

parts.note: free means unconfined

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the word is reads from bottom to top

parts.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: A flower, free to grow, is springing up all over Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so Austria's letter sits at the very bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant from southern Africa.

clue.text: Almost all cricket side run out — quick stuff?

indicators.note: almost takes the last letter off the word all

parts.note: taken as written
the leg side is one half of a cricket field
RO is the scorecard abbreviation for run out in cricket

explanation.surface: Nearly the whole cricket team is run out, quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs. Allegro is a musical direction meaning fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning brisk and lively, so music played fast.

clue.text: Molten metal core? One's not present at the outset

definitions.text: One's not present at the outset

indicators.note: molten means melted, so the letters are melted down and recast

explanation.surface: A geologist ponders a planet's molten metal core.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a riddle: someone who arrives after the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who arrives after things have begun is not there at the start.

clue.text: See 24
Extra luxurious? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for luxurious loses its final letter

parts.note: plush means luxurious

explanation.surface: An additional luxury that is only partly lavish.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUSH loses its last letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added as a bonus is an addition or extra.

clue.text: Pipe associated with area of Scotland

explanation.surface: A bagpipe associated with a Scottish region.
explanation.definitionFit: A small high-pitched flute played in military bands; also a council area of eastern Scotland north of Edinburgh.

clue.text: See 16 down
Approaching new trial in part of London

indicators.note: in part of London, the Cockney East End, speakers drop the h, so the word for trial loses its first letter

parts.note: a hearing is a trial in court

explanation.surface: A new court case is coming up in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys of London's East End drop their aitches, so HEARING becomes 'EARING.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming close to something, as a deadline, is drawing near.

clue.text: One circumvents hard stony beach

indicators.note: circumvents literally means goes around, so the word for one surrounds the hard letter

parts.note: single means one
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone makes their way around a hard, pebbly beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circumvents' usually means dodging, but here it means going round.
explanation.definitionFit: Small rounded pebbles on a seashore make a pebbly beach.

clue.text: Somehow like clothes shoppers?

explanation.surface: Shoppers for clothes get it right somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: Shoppers hunting for the latest style are literally chasing a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Means in some way, not very well; and literally seeking a trend, like style-chasing buyers.
